findings.evidence: Claim 'adds no test ... none exists elsewhere' is a misread. The PR's only test-carrying change is the bump of the private sqlglot-integration-tests submodule (fivetran/sqlglot-integration-tests per .gitmodules; git log shows prior commits 'Sync w/ integration tests'). The submodule is empty in the checkout, so the model could not see the tests; the diff deleting the clickhouse unit cases is consistent with them being re-homed there. O3 ('a AND (b OR c)' regression) is speculative: the final commit message says 'remove the interval logic', so the FUNC_TOKENS-vs-interval concern no longer applies. Cannot prove the submodule holds the cases, but the model's own not_reviewed note admits it never saw the submodule contents and still asserted high confidence.
findings.skeleton_ok: plausible but unverifiable (model itself says expected outputs must be confirmed); redundant if the submodule has the cases

findings.evidence: Same root cause. The diff does delete 5 clickhouse validate_identity cases from tests/dialects/test_clickhouse.py and the output changes to Paren, so 'tests deleted' is factually true, but the author evidently moved/updated them via the submodule bump; the comment tells the author to re-add tests they very likely already wrote. findings.evidence: The PR is a mechanical sweep of ~25 for...in loops to Object.entries/keys and adds eslint rule 'guard-for-in': 'error' (eslint.config.js in diff), which statically blocks a revert; a unit test for one of 25 loops is redundant. Existing tests already pollution-check this file (rpc-json-serializer.test.ts:384-385, 428-434, 457-468) though none sets an inherited enumerable key, so 'reverting to for...in passes all tests' is technically true. The skeleton is BROKEN: it does `const [json] = serializer.serialize(...)` but the file uses `const { json, meta, maps, blobs } = serializer.serialize(...)` (line 60), so it throws 'not iterable'.

Clone is documented 'exists for testing' and only called from Test_Snapshot_Clone (state_test.go:53-97, which covers missing-source + success only). The branch is untested, but snapshotName(term,index) (store.go:960) embeds time.Now() in milliseconds, so the destination id differs on every call and the 'already exists' branch is practically unreachable (only a same-millisecond collision). The suggested skeleton calls Clone twice with the same index/term and asserts the second errors; it will almost always get nil and FAIL or be flaky, so the comment is actively misleading.

True that Test_Snapshot_Clone asserts only Index/Term via List and never compares copied data/CRC sidecars. But Clone is a test-only helper, fsutil.CopyDir is a pass-through, and downstream tests using clones would fail on empty snapshots. Real but not worth a comment. Body names a concrete mutation ('dropping the copy would still pass') but gives prose only.

Repo-wide grep of *_test.go: fatalFn appears only in store_test.go:950/979 (Reap corruption tests) and sink_test.go:329; Verify()/ensureVerified/verifyErr have zero test callers. Corruption tests are Test_Store_ReapCorruptDB/WAL only. The PR also removed Check()'s CRC pass and the Check() calls in tests, so deleting the ensureVerified call in Open() leaves everything green. Concrete production impact: corrupt snapshot streamed to a peer or restored.
